outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each of the 141 markers is an individual sample measurement (rhythmicity index vs. period), not an aggregated average; scatter plots of raw individual points are exempt from this check.

Each marker represents the mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter/cell line (per caption), i.e. an averaged value with error bars, but the underlying individual replicate measurements are not shown.
These are density/distribution curves (line plots) showing normal/gamma distributions of subtype-averaged parameters; line/distribution plots are exempt from needing individual point overlays.
This is a boxplot (median, IQR, whiskers), which is already exempt as it displays the data distribution; in addition, individual sample data points are overlaid on the boxes.
Polar histograms display the distribution of phase-difference values (binned frequency/probability), analogous to a histogram, and are not simple averages requiring individual point overlays.
Polar histogram showing binned distribution of subtype-averaged phase differences; as a histogram-type distribution plot it does not require overlaid individual data points.
This is an example line plot/schematic of a single fitted signal illustrating the analysis method, not a plot of averaged data across samples.

Scatter plot where each of the 117 markers represents an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; error bars reflect fitting uncertainty per sample, not averaging across replicates, so it qualifies as a raw-data scatter plot exempt from this check.
